The son will most likely not prevail, so the answer is C. He was an intended donee beneficiary, but under Restatement (Second) of Contracts §311 his rights vest only when he learns of the contract and relies on it, sues, or assents. None of that happened before the owner and landscaper modified the payee, so their modification was effective. My earlier answer of B was wrong because the landscaper's completed performance doesn't vest the son's rights, and the team note that rights vest at signing states the older, minority rule.

CONFIDENCE: 72
